name: Ghana Basic 9 Linear Relations Readiness Map
intended_context: Adaptive mathematics practice supporting Ghana Basic 9 linear-relations learning and preparation for SHS1.
development_context: Initial Ghana curriculum-aligned slice using validated existing STACK questions. Coverage gaps are retained explicitly rather than inferred from loosely related questions.

mappings.learning_outcome: Read and plot Cartesian coordinates as prerequisite evidence for graphing linear relations.

questions.question_name: Writing down coordinates of points in a graph
questions.notes: Existing STACK item used as prerequisite coordinate-reading evidence. It does not by itself establish mastery of B9 simultaneous linear equations.

questions.question_name: Plotting points on a Cartesian plane
questions.notes: Interactive coordinate-plotting evidence used to establish readiness for straight-line graph work.

mappings.source_basis: Existing STACK coordinate questions aligned as prerequisite evidence for Ghana B8-B9 Patterns and Relations.
mappings.reviewer_notes: Prerequisite/remediation content. Curriculum alignment requires educational review before production use.

mappings.learning_outcome: Graph straight-line relations and determine equations of straight lines as preparation for paired linear relations.

questions.question_name: Sketching straight-line graphs y = mx + c
questions.notes: Direct evidence for straight-line graphing and the y = mx + c representation.

questions.question_name: Determining the equation of a straight line
questions.notes: Readiness mastery evidence for determining a straight-line equation. This does not assess graphical solution of two simultaneous equations.

mappings.source_basis: Existing STACK straight-line questions aligned with Ghana B8 straight-line foundations and B9 readiness requirements.
mappings.reviewer_notes: Strong prerequisite/readiness coverage, but not sufficient evidence for the complete B9 linear-relations standard.

mappings.learning_outcome: Construct and graph two linear relations and use their point of intersection to solve simultaneous linear equations.

questions.question_name: Complete a table for a linear relation
questions.notes: Direct Ghana B9 item aligned to B9.2.1.1.1. Learners complete a table of values for a linear relation. This begins direct coverage of the B9 simultaneous-equations progression but does not yet establish full mastery of the concept.

questions.question_name: Complete a partially filled linear-relation table
questions.notes: Shared curriculum-independent question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.1. Learners interpret a linear relation not initially solved for y and complete missing values in a partially populated table.

Shared curriculum-independent question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.1. Learners complete selected outputs for two distinct linear relations using common x-values and receive diagnostic feedback when the wrong relation is used.

questions.question_name: Complete tables from different linear representations
questions.notes: Shared curriculum-independent procedural question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.1. Learners work with two linear relations in different algebraic forms and must correctly interpret and rearrange the second relation before completing its table.

Shared curriculum-independent visual question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.1. Learners graph two distinct linear relations on the same Cartesian plane using draggable point pairs.

questions.question_name: Graph relations from a table and equation
questions.notes: Shared curriculum-independent visual question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.1. Learners graph two linear relations represented in different forms: Relation A from a table of values and Relation B from an equation. The task adds representational translation evidence beyond QLIN-05.

questions.question_name: Read missing coordinates from two linear graphs
questions.notes: Shared curriculum-independent conceptual question mapped as direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.2. Learners interpret two fixed linear graphs and complete missing coordinates in ordered pairs. The task adds graph-reading and coordinate-interpretation evidence without requiring learners to construct the lines.

questions.question_name: Identify the intersection of two linear graphs
questions.notes: Direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for identifying the common solution of two linear relations from their graph intersection.

questions.question_name: Interpret the intersection of two service plans
questions.notes: Direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for interpreting both coordinates of the intersection of two linear relations in a real-world context.

Direct Ghana Basic 9 evidence for B9.2.1.1.3. Learners construct both linear graphs from their equations on the same Cartesian plane and use the point of intersection as the graphical solution of the simultaneous equations.

questions.question_name: Model and solve two service plans graphically
questions.notes: Direct Ghana Basic 9 challenge evidence for B9.2.1.1.3. Learners translate two contextual linear relationships into equations, construct both graphs, identify their intersection, and interpret both coordinates in the original context. This extends QLIN-10 by requiring the equations to be formed before graphical solution.

questions.question_name: Complete tables, graph two relations, and solve simultaneous equations
questions.notes: Final integrated Ghana Basic 9 mastery evidence for B9.2.1.1.1, B9.2.1.1.2, and B9.2.1.1.3. Learners complete values in two linear-relation tables, construct both graphs, identify their intersection, and state the simultaneous-equation solution. The item has been validated against live STACK grading with diagnostics for wrong-relation table entries, graph errors, duplicate points, swapped lines, reversed intersections, and incorrect final solutions.

mappings.source_basis: Ghana Basic 9 Patterns and Relations requires graphical solution of simultaneous linear equations.
mappings.reviewer_notes: Direct coverage now progresses from tables and algebraic representations through graph construction, graph reading, intersection identification, contextual interpretation, graphical solution, harder context-to-equation-to-graph reasoning, and a final integrated table-to-graph-to-intersection mastery check. QLIN-12 is the required mastery evidence for this Ghana Basic 9 linear-relations slice.
